title: Cap. 6 Arg. 7: They reverse the order—obstacle cleared because efficacious grace was given
pass_a_gloss: As if they were saying that grace in this or that particular person is efficacious because he himself did not oppose an obstacle: whereas they ought to have said that for this reason he did not oppose an obstacle, because God according to his good pleasure gave him efficacious grace. Now indeed I join on the Minor, and I affirm that it is utterly alien from Theology and from truth if anyone maintains that by the death of Christ such a decree has been established, according to which the certain attainment of grace and of salvation is recalled from the absolute will of God to the free choice of the human will.
pass_b_english: As if they said grace is efficacious in this or that particular person because he himself raised no obstacle—when they ought to have said he raised none because God, of his good pleasure, gave him efficacious grace. I now add the Minor, and I affirm it is wholly alien to theology and to truth for anyone to hold that Christ's death established a decree by which the sure attainment of grace and salvation is shifted from God's absolute will onto the free choice of the human will.
source_text: Quasi dicerent, gratiam in hac vel illa persona singulari esse efficacem, quia ipse obicem non opposuit: cum dicere debuissent, ideo obicem non opposuisse, quia Deus pro beneplacito suo dederit illi gratiam efficacem. Jam vero adjungo Minorem, & affirmo, esse a Theologia & veritate prorsus alienum, si quis tueatur Christi morte tale decretum stabilitum, juxta quod, certa gratiae & salutis adeptio ab absoluta Dei voluntate ad arbitrium humanae voluntatis revocetur.
